name: Luck applies its interrupted mana regeneration aura natively (#2963)
contract: Spell.dbc gives both Luck ranks a single self-targeted APPLY_AURA effect of aura 134 SPELL_AURA_MOD_MANA_REGEN_INTERRUPT: 706085 has EffectBasePoints 39 with DieSides 1 -> 40, and 707828 has 79 -> 80. The 706085 tooltip reads 'Allows 40% of your mana regeneration to continue while in combat' (its AuraDescription says 'while casting'; the core implements the interrupted/five-second-rule regeneration, which matches the aura type and the aura description). The aura type has a real handler: AuraEffect::HandleAuraModRegenInterrupt -> Player::UpdateManaRegen, which clamps GetTotalAuraModifier(SPELL_AURA_MOD_MANA_REGEN_INTERRUPT) at 100 and writes power_regen_mp5 + CalculatePct(power_regen, modManaRegenInterrupt) into UNIT_FIELD_POWER_REGEN_INTERRUPTED_FLAT_MODIFIER. No script or SQL is needed; this is a regression scenario for behaviour that already works. COVERAGE LIMIT: this scenario proves the DATA half only - that each rank applies and resolves to 40 and 80. The regeneration itself lands in UNIT_FIELD_POWER_REGEN_INTERRUPTED_FLAT_MODIFIER and the harness exposes power only as net state, which also moves with absorbs, procs and other effects; a power-delta observation would not discriminate, so none is written here. A decisive assertion needs a power_regen_interrupted metric added to CoAGameplayTest.cpp.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
No Luck aura before the passive is learned
Learning the first rank applies its aura
First rank resolves to 40 (data only, see contract)
Learning the second rank applies its aura
Second rank resolves to 80 (data only, see contract)
